long_biography.plain_text:
When Mexican businessman Ricardo Salinas Pliego took charge of the family retailer Elektra in 1987, it had 59 outlets and serious financial problems. He narrowed its merchandise to household essentials and restored instalment sales with stricter risk controls. The store network then became a distribution system for Banco Azteca, bringing savings, credit, pensions and insurance to customers beyond conventional bank channels.

The 1993 acquisition of two state television licences created TV Azteca and challenged Mexico's long-standing television monopoly. Salinas later established Fundación Azteca, whose work has included schools, scholarships and cultural and environmental programmes. He has also used his personal publishing and speaking platforms to advocate entrepreneurship, education and economic liberty.
